title: Gabber finite cover of a modified closed image
statement: Let $g:F'\to S$ be a proper morphism of reduced Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $F\subset S$ be its closed image with the reduced induced structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exist a blowup $p:S'\to S$ with nowhere dense centre, which is a modification [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data], and an $F$-scheme $G$ with an $F$-morphism $G\to F'$ and a finite surjective $F$-morphism $G\to F\times_S S'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1, pp. 7--8 (Gabber). Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Write $F$ for the reduced closed image of $g$. The map $g$ factors through $F$: on affine charts every function in the radical ideal of the image pulls back to a function vanishing at every point of the reduced scheme $F'$, hence to zero. For every integral closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow F$, apply [lem-trf-closed-image-generic-alteration] to $g:F'\to S$ and $Z\hookrightarrow S$. It gives an integral closed subscheme $W_Z\hookrightarrow F'$ and an alteration $W_Z\to Z$ whose composite with $Z\hookrightarrow S$ is the restriction of $g$ to $W_Z$; since $F\hookrightarrow S$ is a monomorphism, $W_Z\to Z\hookrightarrow F$ is also the restriction of the factored map $F'\to F$.

Apply [lem-trf-alteration-blowup-finite] to each alteration $W_Z\to Z$. Obtain a nowhere dense closed center $R_Z\subsetneq Z$, the blowup $\widetilde Z=\operatorname{Bl}_{R_Z}(Z)\to Z$, a blowup modification $\widetilde W_Z\to W_Z$, and a finite surjective map $\widetilde W_Z\to\widetilde Z$ over $Z$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8 (author PDF lines 674--676), using Lemma 2.5 on p. 4

proof.text: The locally closed subsets $Z\setminus R_Z$ cover $F$: a point of $F$ lies in the integral closed subscheme given by the closure of that point, and it is outside the corresponding proper closed subset $R_Z$. Because $F$ is Noetherian, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and therefore spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Each $Z\setminus R_Z$ is constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset], hence open in the constructible topology by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-clopen-constructible-topology]. The constructible topology is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact], so finitely many pairs $(Z_i,R_{Z_i})$, $i=1,\ldots,r$, cover $F$.

View each $R_i:=R_{Z_i}$ as a closed subscheme of $S$, with ideal $\mathcal J_i$, and put $S_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{R_i}(S)$ and $U=S\setminus\bigcup_i|R_i|$. Each $R_i$ avoids every generic point of $S$: if such a point lay in $R_i\subset Z_i$, the integral closed $Z_i$ would be that irreducible component of $S$, whereas a proper closed subset $R_i$ of $Z_i$ cannot contain its generic point. Thus $U$ is dense and quasi-compact. All $\mathcal J_i$ are finite-type quasi-coherent ideals since $S$ is Noetherian, and restrict to the unit ideal on $U$. Iterating [lemma-nagata-product-ideal-common-blowup] gives $S'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\prod_i\mathcal J_i}(S)$ and maps $q_i:S'\to S_i$ over $S$. Its center is nowhere dense, and it is an isomorphism over $U$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open]. It is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], and its inverse image of $U$ is dense by [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup]. Hence it is a modification by [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. If $F$ is empty, take the empty product ideal $\mathcal O_S$, so $S'=S$, and take $G=\varnothing$; this already proves the conclusion in that case.

Let $H=F\times_S S'$ and give every irreducible component $T_j\hookrightarrow H$ its reduced induced structure, so $T_j$ is integral. Write $\eta_j$ for its generic point and $x_j$ for the image in $F$. Choose $i=i_j$ with $x_j\in Z_i\setminus R_i$ using Step 3. By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed], the blowup $\widetilde Z_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{R_i}(Z_i)$ is a closed subscheme of $S_i$, with the indicated map to $Z_i\hookrightarrow S$. The map $S_i\to S$ is an isomorphism over $V_i=S\setminus|R_i|$ by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], applied to $V_i$, since its center avoids $V_i$. Applying the same statement to $\widetilde Z_i\to Z_i$ over $Z_i\setminus|R_i|$ identifies the restriction of this closed subscheme in $S_i$ with $Z_i\setminus R_i$. Consequently $h_j(\eta_j)\in|\widetilde Z_i|$ for $h_j:T_j\hookrightarrow H\to S'\xrightarrow{q_i}S_i$.

We now obtain the scheme-theoretic factorization of $h_j$, not merely a containment of points. Let $\mathcal K_i$ be the ideal of the closed immersion $\widetilde Z_i\hookrightarrow S_i$. On any affine open $A\subset S_i$ and nonempty affine open $B\subset h_j^{-1}(A)$, a section of $\mathcal K_i(A)$ maps to zero in $\kappa(\eta_j)$, because the field-valued map at $\eta_j$ factors through that closed subscheme by Step 5. Since $T_j$ is integral, $\mathcal O_{T_j}(B)$ is a domain with fraction field $\kappa(\eta_j)$, so this section already maps to zero in $\mathcal O_{T_j}(B)$. Thus the pulled-back ideal is zero on an affine cover. The quotient-ring maps define a unique morphism $a_j:T_j\to\widetilde Z_i$ with $\iota_i a_j=h_j$; uniqueness makes these local maps glue. Its composite to $S$ equals the given map from $T_j$, since the closed immersion $\iota_i$ and $q_i$ are over $S$. The maps $T_j\to Z_i$ obtained through $a_j$ therefore give its prescribed $F$-structure, since $F\hookrightarrow S$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8, lines 687--694: full affine ideal argument for the asserted map to the strict transform.

proof.text: For the morphism $a_j$ constructed in Step 6, form $G_j=T_j\times_{\widetilde Z_i}\widetilde W_{Z_i}$, with projections $b_j:G_j\to T_j$ and $c_j:G_j\to\widetilde W_{Z_i}$. By definition this is the cartesian square whose bottom map is $a_j:T_j\to\widetilde Z_i$ and right map is the finite surjective $\widetilde W_{Z_i}\to\widetilde Z_i$ of Step 2. Its left map $b_j$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The composite $G_j\xrightarrow{c_j}\widetilde W_{Z_i}\to W_{Z_i}\hookrightarrow F'$ gives the other required map. This composite is an $F$-morphism for the $F$-structure through $b_j$: by Step 1, $G_j\to W_{Z_i}\to F'\to F$ equals $G_j\to W_{Z_i}\to Z_i\hookrightarrow F$; by Step 2 this is $G_j\to\widetilde Z_i\to Z_i\hookrightarrow F$; by the cartesian square it is $G_j\xrightarrow{b_j}T_j\xrightarrow{a_j}\widetilde Z_i\to Z_i\hookrightarrow F$, which is the $F$-structure of $T_j$ by Step 6.

The blowup $S'$ is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $S$, so $H=F\times_S S'$ is Noetherian and has only finitely many irreducible components $T_j$. Put $G=\coprod_jG_j$. Its map to $H$ is finite: on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset H$, write $T_j\cap\operatorname{Spec}A=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_j)$; the inverse image in $G_j$ is affine with coordinate ring $B_j$ finite over $A/I_j$, hence finite over $A$. The whole inverse image in $G$ is the spectrum of the finite product $\prod_j B_j$, a finite $A$-module. The images of the surjections $G_j\to T_j$ cover $H$, so $G\to H$ is surjective, even if $H$ is nonreduced. The $F$-maps $G_j\to F'$ assemble into an $F$-map $G\to F'$, proving the claim.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 3.2.1 (Gabber), pp. 7--8; proof lines 668--699 in the author PDF

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_cover_modified_closedImage {S F' : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced S] [IsNoetherian S] [IsReduced F'] [IsNoetherian F'] (g : F' ⟶ S) [IsProper g] (F : Scheme.{u}) (i : F ⟶ S) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsReduced F] (himage : Set.range i = Set.range g) (factor : ∃ gF : F' ⟶ F, gF ≫ i = g) : ∃ (I : S.IdealSheafData), IsNowhereDense (I.support : Set S) ∧ IsModification I.blowupMap ∧ ∃ (G : Scheme.{u}) (gG : G ⟶ F), ∃ (a : G ⟶ F') (q : G ⟶ pullback i I.blowupMap), a ≫ g = gG ≫ i ∧ q ≫ pullback.fst i I.blowupMap = gG ∧ IsFinite q ∧ Surjective q
